column6: Said both Chaitin's theorem and the halting problem "follow from" the uncomputability of K(x); plain uncomputability of K does not imply Chaitin's theorem. Softened to "connects to". OLD TEXT: Explainer says Omega encodes "every finite mathematical problem" (overstated; it settles Pi_1-type questions such as halting).
Chaitin bullet dropped the qualifier: an inconsistent system proves everything. Added "sound formal system with computably listable axioms".
OLD TEXT: Q3 ABAC answer is wrong. From [0.36,0.468), C selects [0.4572,0.468), width 0.0108 = 0.6*0.3*0.6*0.1 (not 0.006); -log2(0.0108) = 6.53 bits.
Repetition-3 at p=0.1: rate 1/3, error 0.028, checked.

OLD TEXT, serious: Q2 (true-false) answer "true" is wrong; superposition beats time-sharing and the region is not a triangle. Q4 explanation contains drafting chatter ("Hmm... let me recalculate... I'll mark option") and no option matches (correct R_2 = 0.5*log2(1+4/(6+4)) = 0.24, R_1 = 1.40). Q1 option uses wrong formula. Explainer credits the BC-MAC duality to Bergmans (it is Jindal-Vishwanath-Goldsmith / Vishwanath-Jindal-Goldsmith, 2003-04) and says "cloud cloud".

Correction said superposition coding is "not enough" when receivers are better on different frequencies; for parallel Gaussian BCs, per-subchannel superposition coding does reach capacity (Tse 1997). Replaced with the certain claim that no single ranking holds across the band. Same overclaim sits in the OLD Explainer paragraph 4.

They differ when X and Y share a confounder was absolute (they can coincide; they also differ under reverse causation). Now "They can differ, for example when...". OLD TEXT: Q2 is a "Why...?" question typed true-false.
Exercise fails when worked: Huffman on random letters still saves bits against 8-bit ASCII, so savings do not vanish. Changed "random characters" to "uniformly random bytes".
Worked: h = 2, 0, -2 bits; quantized entropies 1, 2, 3 match h + log2(1/delta).

MI and KL keep their discrete properties overstated: continuous MI can be infinite and has no H-based upper bound. Now names the two properties that do carry over. OLD TEXT: Core Idea says MI is "always non-negative and finite" (I(X;X) is infinite for continuous X).
Worked |X|=8: bound 0.109 bits at P_e=0.01, 1.72 bits at P_e=0.3.
Checked {0.3,0.3,0.2,0.2} gives all 2-bit codewords.
OLD TEXT: Q1 calls the Levi-Civita connection "(flat connection)"; it is not flat in general (the normal family has curvature -1/2).
Checked d(2 arcsin sqrt p)/dp = 1/sqrt(p(1-p)).

If two parameter values give the same distribution, the Fisher matrix is singular is false (e.g. label swap in a mixture). Singularity comes from a local direction that leaves the distribution unchanged; reworded to that.
OLD TEXT, serious: Q1 claims I(S;R)=0 differs from independence and marks that option correct; its own explanation then says independence is exactly what I=0 means. Option 0 is the right answer.
OLD TEXT: Core Idea credits uncomputability of K to "Chaitin's incompleteness results" and calls it "deeper than the halting problem"; loose.

Exercise fails when worked: time-sharing at fixed power is the straight line between single-user points and never touches the sum-rate line. Replaced with the FDMA curve (full power in each band share), which touches it at alpha = P_1/(P_1+P_2) = 10/11. Checked corners: (1.73, 0.063) and (1.29, 0.5); sum 1.79. OLD TEXT: Core Idea says Gaussian sum capacity is log2(1+sum P/N) (missing 1/2 for real channels) and that it is "achieved by the orthogonal multiple access of users alone".
Checked binary adder: I(X1;Y|X2)=1, H(Y)=1.5.
Checked Y=X^2: Cov=0, I = H(1/3,2/3) = 0.918 bits.
